speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Good afternoon, everyone. Raise your hand if you  have a question. We'll try to come to as many as  
we can. Okay, we'll kick off with Alex from the  BBC. Hi. A huge win, dramatic moment in the title  
race and a way for you to get it as well. You  seemed pretty certain from the moment that West  
Ham goal went in that it was a foul, but were you  nervous at all? Well, yeah, what a moment. What an  
afternoon. What a week it's been for us, so full  of emotions. I cannot praise enough the attitude,  
the desire, the courage and the quality the  team has shown throughout this week, because  
there was so much at stake. And today we knew,  against a team that is fighting for their life,  
a club with an incredible history, how tough  it was going to be. I think we started the  
game so well. We created three big chances to  go in front and we didn't manage to do that,  
so we had to keep our heads cool. Then we  had Ben White's injury and we had to make an  
adjustment there. After half-time we had to make  another one with Ricky's injury. And after that,  
I said at half-time to the boys: we're really  going to go for it, so be ready, because if the  
game is not panning out in the manner that we  have to, we're going to have to change it. And  
the finishers have made the difference. Martin  coming in had an incredible impact in the game,  
an action that leaves Leo in a top position to  score the goal. And after that there are two  
moments. One is the save at 0-0, one against one,  which is the story of the season again. And the  
other one is in the most chaotic circumstances,  when two teams are playing for their lives,  
a call from the refs that I think is very brave  but very consistent with what they've been talking  
about all season. So when I have to be critical,  I have been, and today I have to praise them,  
at least for giving the option to a referee  to decide away from the light and the chaos,  
to give clarity to him to make the right call. And  I think when you look at the action in that way,  
I think it is an obvious error and it is a  free-kick and the goal has to be disallowed.  
So congratulations, because they made a big call  in very, very difficult circumstances. John,  
I think it's been described on TV as arguably the  biggest VAR decision in Premier League history,  
which is a fair shout, but also there's no doubt  in your mind that it's a foul. And then I guess a  
lot of people would be thinking, why does it kind  of take so long? Do you understand that? And then  
also, did it add to your tension and nervousness?  Probably today I realised how difficult and how  
big the referee's job is, because you're talking  about a moment that can decide the history,  
the course of two massive clubs that are fighting  with their lives to achieve their objectives. The  
pressure is huge. He was the right choice. Just  quickly, about Ben White. He looked in quite a lot  
of discomfort. Yeah, we don't know, but it doesn't  look good at all. He needs some further testing  
tomorrow probably and I will know a bit more. And  can I also just ask you more generally, apart from  
the game itself, it felt like such a big hurdle  to get over this one at the end of this week.  
Knowing exactly what's in front of you now, how do  you feel? How do they in the dressing room feel?  
Amazing. I feel so happy, so proud. Relief as  well, because we knew the difficulty of the game,  
but we've done it. It's been a phenomenal week  in every sense, what the team is doing, the way  
we play, the way we have approached games, then  what our supporters have done for us this season,  
all week and today as well, is phenomenal. I  think it changes the energy of the team. And  
yeah, we have to live the present now and  just think about Burnley, because that's the  
only important thing. It sounds like you had to  make the change to bring Cristhian Mosquera on,  
but did you feel like moving Declan to right-back  maybe didn't work as well as you expected,  
as well as it had worked? There are two actions  defensively that we suffer a little bit. I don't  
think it's because of his position, but we altered  things. We had to. But as well, with the game that  
I expected, bringing Mosquera was going to unlock  something that we really believed could give us  
the fluidity and the chance to hurt them. But  sometimes you have to make another change. And  
the one on Zubimendi was tough, but I really felt  that we had to put two attacking midfielders in  
that moment to generate all kinds of issues and  threats. And thank God, it did work out. Often  
you think about games where you might score  a lot of goals, momentum from that. Can games  
like this that end in such a way give you such an  emotional feeling and actually be more beneficial,  
especially when there are only two games to go  after that? We created some big chances and we  
didn't score, and the team had to stay cool. I  knew that they were going to have moments as well,  
because they don't need much to create issues in  and around your box with the players that they  
have and the set-up that they have. So, yeah, we  navigated through that and I think we deserved to  
win again. Okay, last two because Nuno's waiting.  We'll go to Nick from Hayters. A couple of those  
early chances fell at the end of Trossard. He  hit the post quite early and then had to wait  
so late to get that winner, his first goal in 2026  despite a good run of form recently. Yeah, well,  
there is a player that makes a difference for  us. And he had, as everybody, it's impossible  
to maintain the level, especially what we demand  of our front players. I think recently he's been  
really, really good. I think the games he played  this week have been phenomenal and he has made a  
difference finally. When you talk about magic  moments, this is certainly one, in the most  
needed moment as well, to pull off that save. It  was incredible. I don't know, he's made a few,  
to be fair. But yeah, that tells you how good he's  been. Okay, everyone, thanks very much. Thank you.
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | West Ham United 0-1 Arsenal | Premier League
